D-wave-terms.note: Phase difference defined loosely as a difference in displacements.

D-polarisation.note: Says oscillations in 'one direction'; mark schemes want 'one plane'.

D-refraction.note: Critical angle explained via 90° refraction but not formally defined.

D-workfunction.note: Threshold frequency not phrased as the 'minimum' frequency.

D-errors.note: Errors appendix not in these pages; only passing mentions of inaccuracy.

F-electron-diffraction.note: Graphite diffraction shown; rings shrinking at higher speed never stated.

K-instruments.note: Instruments named; resolution and choosing between them not discussed.

K-method.note: Only skills checklist and brief repeat-reading tips; no variables or range.

K-safety.note: Only wire-snapping eye protection and EHT supply safety mentioned.

K-graph.note: Gradients, tangents, areas taught; graph-drawing appendix A2 not included.

K-uncertainty.note: Uncertainty appendix A3 is outside these pages.

n2.note: Book also stresses F = ma is only the constant-mass special case.

n3.note: Formal statement omits 'same type'; it appears in the next paragraph. Add it to the definition.

elastic-col.note: Given as a table row (kinetic energy conserved), not a sentence.

inelastic-col.note: Table row only; state that kinetic energy is not conserved while total energy is.

moments.note: Book says 'rotational equilibrium'; plain 'equilibrium' is fine.

equilibrium.note: Book says net force and net moment are zero; add 'about any point'.

cog.note: Book attaches the 'weight appears to act' wording to centre of mass; same point here.

terminal.note: Opening sentence says drag 'balances' weight; write resultant force zero, so velocity constant.

hooke.note: Book uses elastic limit as the boundary; limit of proportionality is more precise.

displacement.note: Book only says displacement is a vector; define it as distance in a stated direction.

accuracy.note: Not defined in these pages: accuracy means close to the true value, precision means small spread.

errors.note: Not defined: systematic shifts all readings the same way; random scatters readings either side.

resistivity.note: Write it as RA/L for a component of that material; give the unit Ω m.

kirchhoff1.note: Formal statement says 'any point'; examiners expect 'junction'. Junction appears later on p183.

numdensity.note: Keep 'free' and 'per unit volume'; avoid plain 'electrons per cubic metre'.

drift.note: Term used in I = Anev but never defined: average velocity of charge carriers along the conductor.

wave-terms.note: Peak-to-peak given as an example; lead with minimum distance between adjacent points in phase.

phase-diff.note: Book calls it a difference in displacements; state the fraction of a cycle between two points, in degrees/radians.

polarised.note: Book says oscillations in 'one direction only'; say oscillations confined to one plane.

interference.note: Book's sentence omits coherence; add superposition of coherent waves giving a stable pattern.

refractive.note: Given as n = c/v; say it in words with 'in a vacuum'.

critical.note: Never formally defined; state the angle of incidence giving a 90° angle of refraction.

threshold.note: Book says emission only 'above a certain frequency'; state minimum frequency of radiation to emit electrons.

findings.title: The book covers the content; it doesn't teach the exam
findings.body: 99 of 109 knowledge items are fully taught and every spec sub-section has pages. What the book lacks is exam technique: precise mark-scheme wording, practical analysis, uncertainty, and the question styles the papers use.

findings.title: The book's practice is easier and calculation-heavy
findings.body: A third of the book's questions are single-step calculations (vs 14% of exam parts). Half are easy (vs 39% in exams) and only 7% hard (vs 10%). The exams lean on show-that, explanation, graph reading and recall in ways the book rarely practises.

findings.title: Whole question styles are missing from the book
findings.body: No six-mark extended responses (17% of Paper 2), almost no multiple choice (1% vs 27% of exam parts), almost no uncertainty work (0.7% vs 5.8% of parts) and few linearising tasks (1.2% vs 3.5%).

findings.title: Practical skills are the biggest blind spot
findings.body: Planning, analysis and evaluation (Module 1) carry about 10% of exam marks but under 2% of the book's pages here. The uncertainties appendix is not in your PDF. Use the Techniques lessons and Playbook for this.

findings.title: Some book definitions would lose marks
findings.body: 51 of 65 definitions in the book would score as written. 11 are risky (missing a required key word or using a refused one) and 3 are never defined. The Definitions drill flags each one.

findings.title: The book over-invests in some topics
findings.body: Circuits basics, resistance, charge, vectors, units and work get roughly twice the book space their exam marks justify. Energy stores, photons, density and pressure, and collisions get less space than their marks.

findings.title: About 4,000+ words are never examined
findings.body: Topic-opening stories, two-dimensional collisions (A level only), Millikan's experiment, optical fibres, superconductivity, thin-film interference and other extensions. Read them for interest, not for marks.

findings.title: A few errors to correct
findings.body: Book p.182 (second copy) says e.m.f. is always less than terminal p.d.; it is always more (the first copy is right). The book blurs elastic limit and limit of proportionality in one place, and says repeat readings improve accuracy, which mark schemes do not accept.

use: Use the book to learn and understand content for the first time, topic by topic, then switch to past-paper questions.
Skip or skim the topic-opening stories and the extension boxes listed below.
For definitions, learn the mark-scheme version from the Definitions drill, not the book's wording.
For practical skills and uncertainty, use the Techniques lessons; the book (as you have it) doesn't cover them.
Treat the book's summary questions as warm-ups; they are easier than exam questions.
Spend extra time on topics the book under-weights: photons, energy, density and pressure, collisions, and all of Module 1.

errors.issue: States e.m.f. is always less than the terminal p.d.
errors.fix: E.m.f. is always greater than the terminal p.d. when current flows (lost volts Ir).

errors.issue: Treats the elastic limit as the end of the straight-line region.
errors.fix: The limit of proportionality ends the straight line; the elastic limit can be later.
Repeating and averaging reduces random error and improves precision, not accuracy.
